svg.aria-label: How to write மேலே: 4 parts, ே, ம, ே, ல, one after another
svg.title: Writing மேலே
svg.desc: 4 parts written one after another: ே, ம, ே, ல (tamil). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which is not always the order they are typed: a vowel sign written to the left of its consonant comes before it. Each vowel sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansTamil-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ே: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 42 (ே, ee sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Tamil writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>; ம: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 1 (Univ. of Texas at Austin) <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ே: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 42 (ே, ee sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Tamil writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>; ல: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 9, ல (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 194 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>. Source notes on variation: ே: The recognizer stores native Tamil writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 105 of the 108 stored prototypes of the ee sign (97%) are one pen-down stroke. 104 of those 105 turn counterclockwise: the pen starts in the upper half (98), inside the small upper curl, circles it, sweeps left and down the big curve, and curls up into the lower loop, ending in the lower half (102). The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline. Handwriting varies by writer. ம: Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation; there is no single national stroke-order standard. This is one attested order. ே: The recognizer stores native Tamil writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 105 of the 108 stored prototypes of the ee sign (97%) are one pen-down stroke. 104 of those 105 turn counterclockwise: the pen starts in the upper half (98), inside the small upper curl, circles it, sweeps left and down the big curve, and curls up into the lower loop, ending in the lower half (102). The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline. Handwriting varies by writer. ல: Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation; there is no single national stroke-order standard. This is one attested order.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 parts, one after another
Part 1 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 2 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 5 movements
Part 3 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 4 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 4 movements
Parts 1 and 3: stroke order after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 42 (ே, ee sign): stored
online-handwriting prototypes from native Tamil writers (MIT licence, 2012)
Part 2: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 1 (Univ. of Texas at Austin)
Part 4: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 9, ல (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p.
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
